verdict.rationale: Name.com documents a Core API check-availability endpoint that checks up to 50 domains per call and returns pricing. An official MCP server lets agents call Core API operations, and typed SDKs and a sandbox support integration. However, no evidence in the pack documents rate limits for the endpoint, which the story explicitly requires. Missing for 10: documented rate limits for availability checks, independent or hands-on corroboration of the check endpoint.

support.subject: As a developer, I can check domain availability programmatically — a documented check/search API my code or agent can call with clear rate limits

citations.quote: Checks whether up to 50 domain names are purchasable and returns **discovery** pricing for each result.
The name.com Model Context Protocol (MCP) server lets AI agents (e.g., Cursor, Claude Desktop) safely call name.com Core API operations on your behalf.
Official client SDKs for the name.com Core API. They give you typed clients that map directly to the API reference
